summary.title: Part 6 - Dockerizing your Backend
summary.one_liner: You learn how to containerize a Go WebSocket chat backend with a Dockerfile, build it with the docker CLI, and run it on port 8080.
takeaways: Write a Dockerfile based on golang:1.11.1-alpine3.8 that copies the source, downloads modules, and builds a binary.
Build the image with 'docker build -t backend .' and run it with 'docker run -it -p 8080:8080 backend'.
Docker makes the backend deployable to any Docker-capable host with a single run command, reducing environment mismatch.
The frontend is not containerized because it will be hosted as static files, for example on an AWS S3 bucket.
summary.summary: This is part 6 of a series building a Go and ReactJS chat application. The article explains why Docker helps with consistent deployments, then walks through installing Docker Desktop, writing a Dockerfile for the Go backend, building the image, and running it with a port mapping. It shows sample log output from the running WebSocket server and briefly notes that services like AWS ECS or Google Cloud could host the container. It explains that the frontend is left out of Docker because it will be deployed as built static files.
